specification.problem: Determine the parity (even/odd) of a permutation of 4 elements (S_4) using a single evaluation of a permutation oracle acting on a ququart (4-level system encoded in photon polarization and spatial modes).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest construction: a standard background parity-determining scheme for permutations of {0,1,2,3} on a single ququart, using a tiny explicit instance, with a generic Fourier-type interference measurement. Outside scope: the actual linear-optical implementation (polarization/path encoding, interferometer layout), the paper's exact algorithm, the full set of permutation transformations, experimental fidelities and the speedup claim details.

symbols.meaning: permutation of the four basis labels
ququart basis state, j=0..3 (assumed encoding: 2 polarization x 2 spatial modes)
parity of the permutation, +1 even, -1 odd

equations.label: Permutation action
equations.description: Permutation transformation acting on the ququart basis.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions permutation transformations on ququart states but gives no explicit formula; this is the natural definition.

equations.label: Parity as determinant
equations.description: The parity of a permutation equals the determinant of its permutation matrix.
equations.justification: Standard group-theory fact; the abstract only states that parity is determined in one evaluation.

equations.label: Parity via a Fourier-type input state
equations.description: Illustrative input state; in general parity is not an overlap with a fixed state, so this is only an illustrative choice.
equations.justification: A proposed construction not established by the abstract. The paper's actual input state and measurement are unknown.
assumptions: Illustrative only; not claimed to determine parity for all S_4 elements

equations.label: Single-query distinguishing criterion
equations.latex: \text{parity determined in one query iff } \exists\, M:\ \langle\psi_\sigma|M|\psi_\sigma\rangle \text{ separates even and odd }\sigma,\ |\psi_\sigma\rangle=P_\sigma|\psi_0\rangle
equations.description: Condition for a one-evaluation parity test: the output states for even and odd permutations must be perfectly distinguishable (orthogonal subspaces).
equations.abstract_quote: this work determines the parity of the permutation in only one step of evaluation
equations.justification: Inferred from the one-step claim; the precise states used are not given.
assumptions: Perfect distinguishability needed for deterministic output

registers.name: ququart
registers.size: 2 qubits (4 levels): 1 polarization qubit + 1 spatial-mode qubit
registers.role: Carries the permuted state; assumed ordering |j> = |spatial, polarization> with j=2s+p

specification.initial_state: Not specified in the abstract; an assumed single-photon ququart state |psi_0> (eq_3 is only illustrative).

steps.description: Prepare single photon in ququart state |psi_0> using polarization and spatial modes (assumed).
Apply the permutation transformation P_sigma once (one evaluation).
Measure in a basis that distinguishes even from odd permutations (basis not given in abstract).

specification.measurement: Single-photon detection in an unspecified basis separating even- and odd-permutation outputs; details not given in the abstract.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Map detection outcome to parity label +1/-1 (assumed).
assumptions: Ququart encoded as 2 spatial modes x 2 polarizations
The actual algorithm's input state, measurement basis and any ancilla are not reconstructed
Classical comparison (needing multiple evaluations) is background only
